description: We are from Miri Vocational College, representing the CXYZ Space Pioneer team, which consists of students from various programs and different age groups. We have been passionate about space since we were 6 years old. This group was formed by Cikgu Lizanah because she noticed our curiosity and desire to learn more about outer space. She then invited us to join a space-related competition to create a story that helps children aged 12 and under spark their interest in space.
summary: Sojourner: The First Rover on Mars is an interactive storybook for children, narrated partly by the rover itself. It starts with scientists asking what is hiding on Mars and deciding to send a robot instead of people. Sojourner, named after Sojourner Truth, was built by NASA scientists and engineers with six wheels, cameras, and tools for studying rocks and soil. She launched on 4 December 1996 on a Delta II 7925 rocket, packed inside the Mars Pathfinder spacecraft. After a seven-month trip, Pathfinder landed on 4 July 1997 using a parachute and airbags. Sojourner then rolled off a ramp and explored rocks named Barnacle Bill, Yogi, Wedge, and Casper. Pathfinder relayed her pictures and findings to NASA’s antennas on Earth. She was built to last 7 days but worked for about 83, and Pathfinder’s final message came on 27 September 1997. The mission found pebbles showing that water once flowed on Mars, and it paved the way for Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Perseverance.
details:
🚀 Details

Sojourner: The First Rover on Mars is an interactive digital storybook told from the point of view of the rover Sojourner, with Mars Pathfinder as her partner. In a series of short scenes, the story follows the mission from the build and launch to the landing, the exploration of rocks like Wedge, Casper, Yogi, and Barnacle Bill, and the end of the mission. It blends real NASA mission history with a friendly adventure for young

💻 Tech Stack

  • Canva (interactive website design and publishing)
  • Clickable navigation (Next, Cancel, and Home buttons)
  • Clickable mission control map of the landing site
  • Built-in mini game
  • Shared as a web link, with no installation needed

✨ Innovation Highlights

  • 🤖 Character Narration: The rover tells her own story, which makes ideas like rover, lander, and data relay easy to follow.
  • 🗺️ Mission Control Experience: A map of the real Pathfinder landing site lets learners click locations like a NASA team.
  • 📡 Simple Data Flow: A short diagram shows how pictures travel from Sojourner to Pathfinder to Earth.
  • 🎮 Learn by Playing: A mini game at the end lets learners practise what they learned.
  • 🔁 Reusable Format: The “Lesson 1” layout can be reused for future space lessons.
  • 📚 Trusted Facts: The mission details, dates, and rock names come from NASA’s Mars Pathfinder mission.
